title: tools/call carrying the spec's params._meta is refused as malformed
body:
## Summary
The MCP `Call` struct denies unknown fields, so a spec-valid `tools/call` whose params carry `_meta` (progressToken) is refused `malformed_call`.

## Description
crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:238-242 decodes `params` into `Call { name, arguments }` with `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`. The MCP 2024-11-05 schema (the version the server announces on `initialize`) gives every request's params an optional `_meta` object (progressToken). A client that sends one has EVERY tool call refused, audited as malformed, and the model told its call was malformed. Whether claude-code / codex-cli send `_meta` is UNVERIFIED (.research does not say). Fixed looks like: accept an optional `_meta` object and ignore it; every other unknown field still refused.

## Flow
- engine sends tools/call {name:'table_view',arguments:{},_meta:{progressToken:1}}
- Call decode fails at crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:487 -> RefusalCode::MalformedCall
- record_refusal audits it; the agent gets isError malformed_call; no tool ever runs
- fix: an optional `_meta` object field on Call, ignored; test both shapes

## Expected impact
A live engine whose MCP client attaches _meta can use no tool at all, and the spike would read it as an engine failure. Could break: nothing reads _meta.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - spec-valid tool calls are served
Before: a tools/call with params._meta -> isError malformed_call (walked against crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:238-242, 484-489)
After: the same call -> served; params with any other unknown key still malformed_call
Method: simulation - client behaviour is unverified offline; the server half is a 20-line test the worker writes first
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:237-242 #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] struct Call { name, arguments }
crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:484-487 serde_json::from_value::<Call>(rpc.params.clone()).map_err(|_| RefusalCode::MalformedCall)
instrument: crates/table-mcp/tests/server.rs: tools/call table_view with params._meta {progressToken:1} expects isError false (red today); params.extra still expects malformed_call

title: Refusals the MCP layer makes after invoke are never audited
body:
## Summary
The abandoned-call refusal and the oversized-result refusal are made by the MCP server itself and written to no audit row.

## Description
crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:477-478 says every refusal is audited before the agent hears it, and that refusals past that point are audited by the wallet that made them. Two refusals past that point are made by the MCP layer, not the wallet: the timeout (crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:504-512, Unavailable 'took too long') and the size cap (crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:527-535, 'withheld'). Neither calls record_refusal, and the wallet may meanwhile have SUCCEEDED (its own audit row says so) while the agent was told unavailable. The audit trail cannot show that the agent was told a different outcome from the one the wallet recorded. Fixed: a distinct audit action (mcp.withheld / mcp.abandoned) through AsyncAgentService, not a refusal row that contradicts the wallet's success.

## Flow
- agent calls book_query with a wide view; the wallet answers 80 KB
- crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:527 replaces it with refusal_result(Unavailable, 'withheld')
- audit_log holds the wallet's success and nothing about the withholding
- fix: an audit hook for MCP-layer outcomes, called at both sites; test the call count

## Expected impact
Rewind and audit readers see what the agent was actually told. Could break: audit row counts pinned by tests in table-app / table-runtime.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every agent-visible refusal has an audit row
Before: 2 MCP-made refusal sites, 0 audited (the Slow test service's record_refusal is never reached on either path)
After: 2 of 2 audited, with an action that does not contradict the wallet's own row
Method: simulation - needs a new trait method crossing table-app and table-runtime (ActorBridge); not S
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:477-478 comment: refusals past this point are audited by the wallet
crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:504-512 Err(_) => Err((RefusalCode::Unavailable, 'took too long')) -- no record_refusal
crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:527-535 refusal_result(Unavailable, 'withheld') -- no record_refusal
instrument: crates/table-mcp/tests/server.rs: a counting AsyncAgentService; the bounded() timeout and oversize cases each assert one MCP-layer audit call (0 today)

title: Run directories left by a crashed host are never reaped
body:
## Summary
NativeEngine creates a per-run directory under the app's agents root and removes it only in a Drop; a host crash or kill leaves it forever and nothing sweeps the root at start.

## Description
crates/table-engine/src/native.rs:329-351 RunDirectory::create writes mcp.json, system.md, schema.json and an agent cwd under the shared root; crates/table-engine/src/native.rs:364-389 removes it in Drop (retrying 25 x 20 ms on a thread, then silently giving up). Drop does not run on a crash, a kill or power loss, and NativeEngine::new (crates/table-engine/src/native.rs:54-70) never sweeps stale <uuid> directories. The Job Object kills the children with the host (KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE), so processes are reaped; directories are not. Registry subprocess-lifecycle: 'every child names its reaper ... a startup orphan sweep ... verifying identity'. Both engines share one root (crates/table-runtime/src/engines.rs:96) and a second app instance could too, so the sweep needs a liveness marker (a lock held for the run's life), not a blind delete. Distinct from the recorded test-harness deviation (test scratch roots).

## Flow
- start a native run; kill the host process while the child runs
- the job kills the child; <root>/<uuid>/ with its cwd stays
- next start: NativeEngine::new creates the root and never looks inside it
- fix: a per-run lock file held by the run; new() removes uuid-shaped dirs whose lock is free; test with a seeded stale dir and a held one

## Expected impact
Disk under the app data dir stops growing across crashes; the Drop give-up gets a second chance. Could break: a second instance's live run if the lock is wrong - the test must hold one.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - scratch space is reaped across host crashes
Before: stale run dirs after a crash: never removed (0 sweep sites in the crate)
After: a seeded stale dir is removed by NativeEngine::new; a locked live dir is kept
Method: simulation - walked the create / Drop / new paths; M because it adds a lock protocol
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
crates/table-engine/src/native.rs:63 create_dir_all(&root) -- no sweep
crates/table-engine/src/native.rs:364-389 Drop-only removal, gives up after 25 tries
crates/table-runtime/src/engines.rs:96 both engines on root.clone()
instrument: crates/table-engine/tests/native.rs: seed root/runs/<uuid>/cwd (stale) and a held-lock dir, construct NativeEngine, assert the stale one gone and the live one kept

title: The engine's Job Object sets no process-count or memory budget
body:
## Summary
The kill-on-close Job Object holding every native child sets only JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, so a child tree can spawn and allocate without bound until the 120 s ceiling.

## Description
crates/table-engine/src/windows_job.rs:51 sets LimitFlags = JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE only: no ActiveProcessLimit, JobMemoryLimit or ProcessMemoryLimit. The CLIs are third-party binaries that may load user mods (.research/landscape-and-stack.md 2.1: the CLI permission layer is advisory), on a desktop the wallet shares. Registry subprocess-lifecycle host-resource-protection: 'budgets are per-child ... terminated by policy, not discovered by the host's own death'. Stdout volume is already capped (read_lines, 4 MiB); process count and memory are not.

## Flow
- a child (or a mod it loads) forks repeatedly or allocates several GB
- the job holds them all until the 120 s ceiling, or the machine starves first
- fix: JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_ACTIVE_PROCESS and JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_JOB_MEMORY in the same SetInformationJobObject call
- instrument: engine-fixture modes 'fanout' and 'alloc' the job must stop

## Expected impact
A runaway agent app cannot take the wallet's machine down with it. Could break: a real CLI that legitimately needs more processes - the live spike must confirm the numbers.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - per-child resource budget
Before: job limits: 1 flag (kill-on-close); a fixture spawning 64 descendants keeps all of them alive (walked)
After: fanout past the cap fails to spawn, alloc past the cap is killed; cleanup tests still green
Method: simulation - needs two fixture modes and Win32 limit fields; the numbers need the live spike
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: crates/table-engine/src/bin/engine-fixture.rs modes fanout/alloc + crates/table-engine/tests/native.rs asserting the run ends with the tree dead and memory bounded

title: Every native-run failure collapses into one Process error with no exit code
body:
## Summary
Spawn failure, job-attach failure, a pipe error and a non-zero exit all surface as `Error::Process`, so the run record cannot say which happened.

## Description
crates/table-engine/src/native.rs maps 15+ distinct failures to Error::Process (:173 spawn, :175 job attach, :226-227 stdin, :236-238 a non-zero exit with a clean verdict) and drains stderr to nowhere (:186-194, deliberately: it may hold secrets). crates/table-engine/src/lib.rs Error::Process is a unit variant. Registry subprocess-lifecycle termination-and-reaping: exit honesty - never collapse 'the child ended' into one bucket. A missing binary and a CLI that crashed mid-run both read 'engine process unavailable'. Fixed: a typed cause (spawn, attach, pipe, exit code) carried to the runtime's run-end audit, still with no stderr text.

## Flow
- fixture exits 2 after a clean result line
- crates/table-engine/src/native.rs:237 -> Err(Error::Process)
- the runtime records it exactly like a missing executable
- fix: Error::ProcessExit { code } plus spawn/attach causes; the runtime audit carries the code

## Expected impact
A failed run can be diagnosed from its audit row alone. Could break: exhaustive matches on table_engine::Error in table-runtime.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - failures are distinguishable
Before: 4 failure kinds -> 1 indistinguishable error (walked crates/table-engine/src/native.rs)
After: 4 kinds -> 4 typed causes, exit code recorded, no stderr retained
Method: simulation - the Error enum crosses into table-runtime; M
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
crates/table-engine/src/native.rs:173 spawn().map_err(|_| Error::Process)
crates/table-engine/src/native.rs:175 Job::attach(...) -> Error::Process
crates/table-engine/src/native.rs:236-238 !exit.success() && Clean -> Err(Error::Process)
instrument: crates/table-engine/tests/native.rs: fixture mode 'exit2' after a clean result asserts the error carries code 2; a missing program asserts a distinct spawn cause

title: A codex tool call without arguments passes the parser; a claude one fails
body:
## Summary
The stream parser rejects a claude tool_use with no input as Invalid but turns a codex mcp_tool_call with no arguments into a ToolCall with null arguments.

## Description
crates/table-engine/src/parser.rs:135 `c.get("input").cloned().ok_or(Error::Invalid)?` vs crates/table-engine/src/parser.rs:188 `v.pointer("/item/arguments").cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null)`. One rule (a tool call names its arguments), two implementations, under a crate doc that promises strict stream validation. Whether real codex item.started events always carry `arguments` is not in .research (only the synthetic fixture), so tightening could break a real stream: decide it from a recorded codex stream.

## Flow
- codex emits item.started mcp_tool_call without arguments
- crates/table-engine/src/parser.rs:188 yields ToolCall { arguments: null }
- claude's equivalent yields Err(Invalid) and poisons the run
- fix: ok_or(Error::Invalid) on the codex side once a recorded stream shows arguments is always present

## Expected impact
Both adapters judge the same malformed call the same way. Could break: a real codex stream that omits arguments on item.started.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one rule, one behaviour
Before: claude missing input -> Err; codex missing arguments -> Ok(null) (walked)
After: both -> Err(Invalid); the e1 conformance suite covers the case for both engines
Method: simulation - the premise about codex's real shape needs a recorded stream (spike 1)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: crates/table-engine/tests/engine.rs: e1 suite case 'tool call without arguments' for both engines expecting Err (codex passes today), checked against a recorded codex stream

title: No per-session call budget: a looping model writes an audit row per refusal
body:
## Summary
A grant's session accepts unlimited tool calls for its lifetime, and every refused call appends a hash-chained audit row.

## Description
crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs `handle` checks host, secret, token and expiry, then serves the call; nothing counts calls per session (Session at crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:74-79). Each pre-invoke refusal calls record_refusal (crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:514-516) and each wallet refusal audits too (crates/table-app/src/agent.rs invoke). claude-code is capped at --max-turns 12 but one turn may carry several tool calls, and codex-cli's argv has no turn cap. A model steered by injected counterparty text into a refusal loop grows the append-only audit_log for the whole SESSION_SECS window. Fixed: a per-session call budget after which calls are refused once, coded and audited, and the rest answered without new rows.

## Flow
- the model loops tools/call send_offer outside the band
- each call: a wallet refusal and an audit row
- 120 s of looping -> thousands of rows in an append-only, hash-chained log
- fix: a Session.calls counter; the budget refusal audited once

## Expected impact
One run cannot flood the audit log. Could break: a legitimate long run over the budget - pick it from the playbooks' max rounds.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - bounded audit growth per run
Before: calls per session: unbounded; 1000 malformed calls -> 1000 audit rows (walked)
After: 1000 calls -> budget + 1 rows
Method: simulation - the counting test is S, but the budget number is a policy choice
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:74-79 Session { scope, run, enabled, expires } -- no counter
crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:514-516 record_refusal per refused call
instrument: crates/table-mcp/tests/server.rs: 200 malformed calls on one grant; assert audit rows <= budget + 1 (200 today)

title: Codex's documented item.failed and error events poison a run
body:
## Summary
The codex branch of the stream parser rejects `item.failed` and `item.updated` and treats a non-terminal `error` as the run's end.

## Description
crates/table-engine/src/parser.rs:201-212 makes `error` terminal and crates/table-engine/src/parser.rs:214 `_ => Err(Error::Invalid)` rejects every other type. .research/landscape-and-stack.md:203 lists item.started|item.completed|item.failed as sourced [S] codex events and turn.failed, item.updated, error as recalled [R]. A failed MCP item or a retried-then-recovered stream ends the run as isolation_or_stream_failure. Codex cannot start at all today (no system/init; the probe reports unavailable), so the fix belongs with the attestation redesign and must be decided from a recorded codex stream.

## Flow
- codex reports a failed wallet call as item.failed
- crates/table-engine/src/parser.rs:214 -> Err(Invalid); the run is poisoned
- after a recorded stream: item.failed for a wallet tool -> no event; error terminal only when it really ends the turn

## Expected impact
A codex run survives its own documented events once it can run at all. Could break: the fence, if item.failed can name a non-wallet tool - keep the check.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - documented events do not poison runs
Before: item.failed -> Err(Invalid) (walked)
After: item.failed for a wallet tool -> no event, the run continues
Method: simulation - needs a live codex stream; the operator-only spike 1 is the rung above
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
crates/table-engine/src/parser.rs:201-212 "turn.failed" | "error" => terminal
crates/table-engine/src/parser.rs:214 _ => Err(Error::Invalid)
.research/landscape-and-stack.md:203 item.failed [S]; error, item.updated [R]
instrument: operator-only: scripts/spike.ps1 -Spike 1 recording the codex stream, then a crates/table-engine/tests/fixtures replay
